title: osw-cruiserweight
label: Corg

won.source: promotions/osw/archive/cruiserweight-tournament-final-2002.html (served, primary source)

lost.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "October 19, 2002, Saturday Night Slam, Kid Wonder d. Corg (c) to win the Cruiserweight Title."

how: Won a tournament final over Amy "Aimz" Campbell at Ascension, crowned the first-ever OSW Cruiserweight Champion, after a two-round elimination bracket (beating Lillith in Round One, Aimz beating GV in the other semifinal).
note: First-ever Cruiserweight Champion, per the match's own text ("WINNER, AND NEW OSW CRUISERWEIGHT CHAMPION").

title: osw-cruiserweight
label: Kid Wonder

won.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "October 19, 2002, Saturday Night Slam, Kid Wonder d. Corg (c) to win the Cruiserweight Title." The commentator's line on the 9 Feb 2003 Slam! (/promotions/osw/archive/slam-2003-02-09.html), "a belt he's held for close to four months", fits it.

lost.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "March 16, 2003, Crowning Glory 2 PPV, Tyler Nelson d. Kid Wonder (c) for Soy Boy Memorial Title."

how: Publicly dropped the belt live on the 9 Feb 2003 Slam! (promotions/osw/archive/slam-2003-02-09.html), then reclaimed it on the spot and unilaterally lifted its weight restriction — staged as defiance of PCW's Tyler Nelson, not a formal retirement. The actual win is not separately dated to a served show.
note: Neither the 19 October 2002 Slam nor Crowning Glory 2 is served; the dates are the fed's own title history's. The belt passes to Tyler Nelson as the Soy Boy Memorial Title and continues as osw-united-states.

title: osw-heavyweight
label: Switchblade

won.source: Switchblade's own OSW roster.cgi bio card ("OSW Title History: March 2002, OSW Heavyweight Title"); the fed's own title history and its write-up of Crowning Glory date the win to 10 March 2002 and have him beating Timo Bolamba for the vacant title.

lost.source: The fed's write-up of Slam! 16 and the fed's own title history: Doug Troy beat him for the title.

how: Won the vacant title over Timo Bolamba at Crowning Glory, OSW's debut PPV, 10 Mar 2002; lost it to Doug Troy at Slam! 16, 22 May 2002.
note: First OSW Heavyweight Champion. The roster bio card gave the month only ("March 2002"); the fed's own title history and write-up of Crowning Glory date it to 10 March 2002. Defences on record. Slam!, 23 March 2002: with Drew Hostyle and Frankie Bones against Timo Bolamba and Aimz, the champion's side lost by disqualification and he stayed champion. Slam!, 30 March 2002: a handicap match against two men billed as Timo Bolamba and Aimz, announced as a successful title defence. Slam!, 6 April 2002: against Tempest, who won by disqualification, so the title did not change. Head on Collision, 28 April 2002: beat Ivan Stanislav and was announced as still champion.

how: Won from Heresian Bloodlust (Hessian & Azrael Cain) on 23 June 2002, the same date the pair's own preceding reign ends — closing the chain from Civil Disobedience through Heresian Bloodlust to here.
note: No date connects this reign to Heaven & Hell's later one; that one gap remains. Won the same night as the Cruiserweight tournament final (Ascension, 23 Jun 2002) -- the served page for that date covers the Cruiserweight match, not this tag title win, which has no separate surviving document; linked per the reign-show-linkage convention since it is genuinely the same event. SOURCES DISAGREE: the roster bio cards for Riptah and Short Circuit end the reign on 21 July 2002 and call it a loss; the fed's write-up of Slam! of 20 July 2002 has Commissioner Howard Porter strip Da Westsidaz of the titles without a match, "for failure to fulfill their obligations as champions", and the fed's own title history ends the reign there. This history follows the write-up.

title: osw-united-states
label: Tyler Nelson

won.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "March 16, 2003, Crowning Glory 2 PPV, Tyler Nelson d. Kid Wonder (c) for Soy Boy Memorial Title."

lost.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "May 4, 2003, Sunday Night Slam, Nelson vacates the United States Title on order of Jane Reagan."

how: Won the Soy Boy Memorial Title from Kid Wonder at Crowning Glory 2 and renamed it the United States Title on Sunday Night Slam, 23 March 2003. On the 30 March 2003 Slam (osw-slam-2003-03-30) he is billed "the United States Champion" and keeps it over Scott Taylor, by cheating. Vacated it on order of Jane Reagan on 4 May 2003, a week after winning the World Heavyweight Title from Ivan Stanislav.
note: Neither Crowning Glory 2 nor the 4 May 2003 Slam is served; the dates are the title history's. The 30 March card's own commentary says he "just won the damn title" and shows his "newly fashioned United States title".

title: osw-united-states
label: Politically Incorrect

won.source: The fed's own title history, wrestling site capture of 21 July 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ose-title-history-wrestling-site-july-2003-2003-07-21.html): "May 25, 2003, Sunday Night Slam, Politically Incorrect (William S. Powell and Reginald V. Lovecraft) win the Chaos In The Cage Match and are declared co-holders of the United States Champiobship."

how: Declared co-holders after the Chaos In The Cage match: Powell and Lovecraft, who interfered in the match, made a simultaneous pin on D-Kay Calyx, and because the only rule was that the first pin or submission won, both were named co-titleholders. The fed's lawyers found no proof the match contract was violated (U.S. Title Follow-up, 27 May 2003), so the pair were allowed to defend the belt as a tag team. On 28 May 2003 they handed the belt to OSW officials, refusing to carry a title with the American flag on it, said two new belts were being made, and promised to reveal them on Slam at a first defence against Asa Fountain; no served card shows that defence. Lost it to Azala Zameer at Ascension (osw-ascension-2003-06-29), where they are billed "the OSW American Champions".
note: The 25 May 2003 Slam is not served; the date is the title history's, which the 19 May news post ("Chaos In The Cage to determine the new United States Champion") and the 27 May post ("over the past 36 hours") fit. Lovecraft's card of 24 May 2003 still reads "None in OSW" for titles; the team card of 20 June 2003 reads "OSW United States Champions".

title: osw-united-states
label: Azala Zameer

won.source: Ascension 2003's own text (/promotions/osw/archive/ascension-2003-06-29.html): "Your winner of the match, and NEW OLD SCHOOL WRESTLING AMERICAN CHAMPION...AZALA ZAMEER!"

end.source: Ivan Stanislav's roster card of 13 November 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ivan-stanislav-roster-card-november-2003-2003-11-13.html): "OSW American Champion 8-24-03 - 9-14-03"

how: Won the Contract versus Contract match for the OSW American Championship at Ascension: he drove Lovecraft into the corner with the Spear of Zameer, then pinned Powell after the Ivory Stampede; his own OSW contract was on the line against Lt. Mandela's. His roster card of 8 September 2003 lists "OSE American Championship" under Title History.
note: The end of the reign rests on Ivan Stanislav's card alone: no served show or news post carries the change on 24 August 2003 (the 21 August Overtime card does not mention the belt).

end.source: Ivan Stanislav's roster card of 13 November 2003 (/promotions/osw/archive/ivan-stanislav-roster-card-november-2003-2003-11-13.html): "OSW American Champion 8-24-03 - 9-14-03"
